transcriptText:
Two hands hit the felt. A flush... five cards of one suit. And a full house... three of a kind plus a pair. So which one wins? Make your pick. Flush... or full house? Hold that thought.

Poker has ten hands, and the order never changes. High card. One pair. Two pair. Three of a kind. Straight. Flush. Full house. Four of a kind. Straight flush... and the royal flush on top. But why that order? Deal every possible five cards, nearly two point six million hands, and count each kind. The rare ones finish first.

So, back to your pick. A full house comes up 3,744 ways. A flush... 5,108. Fewer ways means rarer, and rarer ranks higher. The full house wins. It's not about looks. It's counting.

At the table, seven cards can hide two hands. You hold the king and queen of hearts. Three kings jump out first. But look again... five hearts. That's a flush, and it beats three of a kind. So name your hand before you bet. Rarer beats more common. Up next: your best five.
